thread:
marta: Heads up — saw a big p99 jump in the telemetry pipeline around 02:15 UTC. Exporter worker CPU spiked ~3x and queues grew.
raj: Yep. Ingest rate for spans jumped ~18k/s -> ~67k/s for ~3m. exporter queue depth went to max.
raj: quick metrics snippet:
```
span_ingest_rate: 18k/s -> 67k/s
exporter.worker.queue: 512 -> 2048
exporter_cpu: 22% -> 85%
p99_latency: 240ms -> 820ms
```
sasha: Which exporter path is overloaded? otlp-grpc -> s3? compression level?
doug: It's the otlp->s3 archiver. We enabled a routing rule in the checkout canary to send full trace payloads for checkout flows (wanted higher fidelity for payments tracing).
observability-bot: :eyes: deploy-bot reports canary checkout-routing-v2 applied at 02:11 UTC
marta: That routing override would explain the volume. Sending full spans for every checkout trace is a huge delta.
marta: Short term: can we throttle at routing layer or switch that route to sampled=1? Also consider trimming nonessential attributes before export.
raj: Be careful: we saw a strange effect where shrinking batching window made CPU worse (more syscalls + small batch overhead). Current setup is batching.window_ms=50 and batch_size=64 which created many tiny batches after the traffic spike.
raj: Logs show lots of tiny batches and exporter threadpool churn.
sasha: Proposed immediate mitigations:
- revert the checkout full-trace routing override
- increase batching.window_ms to 250ms (coalesce)
- set exporter.max_concurrent_requests to 6
- enable attribute-trim for known heavy keys
```
routing:
  service: checkout
  trace_mode: full  # revert to sample=1
```
doug: I'm going to patch the canary to revert the routing override and apply batching.window_ms=250 + exporter.max_concurrent_requests=6. Rolling now.
deploy-bot: rollback requested by doug at 02:28 UTC — routing override reverted
observability-bot: p99 and exporter CPU trending back down, p99 back to baseline within ~4m of rollback :white_check_mark:
marta: Nice. Longer term: Console should show an "estimated ingest delta" when editing routing/rollout policies (so changes that multiply span volume surface before apply).
marta: Also retention policy note: we're keeping full span bodies for 24h for many services. For high-throughput services we should default to 2h and encourage sampled longer retention.
raj: Agree. Add a preflight model: given historical RPS and rule delta, estimate additional token/span volume and projected exporter CPU. Hook that into rollout UI as a blocker or warning.
sasha: I'll open an RFC and a dashboard tile "Routing Rule Impact" that predicts ingest/cpu delta and shows recent rollouts. Will add a field for recommended default retention.
doug: Action items acked. I'll dump a short runbook for rollback and also add collector-level backpressure to drop noncritical attributes when exporter queue > 75%.
marta: :thumbsup: tagging @oncall FYI
observability-bot: dashboards: https://grafana.internal/redwood/routing-impact (created by sasha)
